scope: One additional authorized streaming pass over a closed original; acquisition/receive window 32.0 to 35.1 simulation seconds; preserve original engineering FAIL

window.inclusion: Event receive time_s or source acquisition_s/stamp_s in window; non-projected track acquisitions only; repeated navigation diagnostics deduplicated by source/fusion/output state

static_fault_schedule.method: Standard-library hashlib reproduction of the read-only frozen frame_dropped formula, not a new simulation or an imported production module
static_fault_schedule.formula: window = stamp_ns // 200000000; score = int.from_bytes(sha256(f"{seed}:{window}".encode()).digest()[:8], "big") / 2**64; drop = score < fraction

diagnostic_conclusions: The strongest supported explanation is the configured deterministic fault schedule: three consecutive 200 ms RGB/depth drop windows from source 34.2 to 34.8 s, matching the missing detector/observation source interval.

The last accepted selected-track measurement is source 34.1 s, committed at observed 34.204 s. Its Mahalanobis squared distance is approximately 0.00821 against threshold 9.21, and its rejected-measurement count is zero. Navigation reference and fusion are also accepted for this source.

The next observed detector/observation acquisition is 34.8 s, delivered at approximately 34.9 s with a confident depth-valid person. The 0.7 s acquisition gap plus approximately 0.1 s observed source-to-delivery interval exceeds the unchanged 0.75 s prediction budget.

The observed safety transition at approximately 34.85 to 34.86 s is consistent with that source-age expiry. No consecutive association/KF gate rejections are shown in the selected-track committed attempts in this window.

After LOST, valid detections return but navigation reports no_accepted_selected_measurement and surface_lost. This is consistent with the existing reselection latch; it does not establish a new standalone navigation-gate failure.
The 10 percent parameter is a fraction of deterministic 200 ms time-window decisions, shared by RGB and depth; it does not promise independent per-frame drops or a maximum outage shorter than 0.75 s.

This diagnoses a continuity-budget exceedance under the existing combined stress configuration. It does not relax any gate, revise the original FAIL, or certify that the tracking task remained continuous.
limitations: Runtime telemetry absence is observed at detector/observation output, not a complete independent ledger of every raw camera and fault-bridge input/output. The deterministic schedule matches and is sufficient to explain the gap, but that ledger was not recorded or read here.

Detector records retain source stamp, completion/delivery time and inference wall duration. Exact detector rgb_received_s, depth_received_s, worker_wait_wall_s and input_age_at_submit_s values were not retained by this bounded extractor; their schema presence alone is not timing evidence.
Matched source/delivery times for surviving frames do not prove that no additional transport, scheduling, synchronization or detector input discard contributed inside the missing interval.
